architecture_models.content: Three governed counting views over shared strict plumbing (bindings, firewall, lifecycle exclusion, UNKNOWN abstention) plus a reputation-only negative control without gates. Beta posterior core with frozen prior/decay grid; EigenTrust power iteration with frozen anchor, damping and convergence rule.

feature_catalog.content: Evidence units in document, span and digest granularity with canonical source, publisher, lineage, independence group and digest bindings; dedup and correlation-cap collapse rules; admit/reject/abstain decisions with reason codes; Beta tails and EigenTrust recommendations kept outside enforcement.

independent_audit.content: Producer path (runner) and audit path (evaluator plus comparison) are independent code reading only raw rows and frozen inputs. A/B series share one commit and tree with distinct process identities; merged verdicts must agree or the series is inadmissible. Limits: tracked-Git evidence only, synthetic corpus, non-blinded holdout.

mathematical_model.content: Beta-Bernoulli conjugacy with uniform prior grid, decay clock, tail event at 0.9 and exact binomial references; EigenTrust row-stochastic fixed point with pre-trusted anchor and damping 0.85; correlation cap at two groups; AUC of tails against admit labels with tails labeled hypothesis quantities.

mental_model.content: Independent weight counts allowed groups, never raw units, digests, URLs or accounts. Unresolved independence abstains instead of inventing a group. Scores rank review queues; only gates admit. Identical text with disjoint transparent provenance keeps full weight.

ontology.content: Unit, source, lineage, group, digest, revocation and decision records per evidence-unit.schema.json; S1-003 lifecycle mapping consumed for exclusion semantics; S1-011 gate mechanics preserved for challenge/retraction handling downstream.

content.Architecture: Evidence units with strict bindings flow through dedup, correlation cap, lifecycle exclusion and the policy firewall; Beta and EigenTrust feed the review queue, never enforcement.
content.Milestones: MVP rule accepted on Phase B canonicalization; production thresholds only after measured calibration data exists.
content.Open decisions: Final numeric threshold after measured data; operator procedures in S1-013; synthesis placement in S1-019.
content.Risks: Novel Sybil shapes evading lineage analysis; uncalibrated threshold promoted to production; reputation mistaken for authorization.
content.Scope: Adopt document-granularity counting with upstream collapse as the calibrated MVP rule; span view for fine-grained revocation; digest view only with bound upstream; reputation outputs stay recommendation-only.
content.Verification: Re-run the frozen matrix with reference tooling; require zero hard violations, probe A-H pass, no sensitivity flips and no UNKNOWN dependence.
content.Workstreams: Wire the frozen contracts into the gate, replay the 72-case matrix for acceptance, calibrate the threshold on dev data in S1-012 follow-up, and hand scoped limits to S1-013 and S1-019.

progress.content: Phase A complete: dependency gate, frozen sources, contracts, 72-case oracle with split manifest, stdlib tooling with green regressions, two process-separated runs, comparison, metrics, probes, sensitivity with joint grid, environment record, decision, calibration limits, S1-011 handoff, native FLOW-11 bundle and derived candidate record. Open: independent re-review, then Phase B canonical round and closure.

research_plan.content: Calibrate evidence granularity, independence and Beta/Sybil behavior for the AgentOS knowledge layer. Frozen contracts, 72-case corpus with lineage-isolated dev/holdout split, three granularity views plus a reputation-only negative control, Beta reference values with metamorphic checks, EigenTrust fixed semantics, probes A-H, joint parameter sensitivity, native FLOW-11 bundle, derived verdict. Phase B canonical round required before closure.

source_registry.content: Six frozen sources across five roles (provenance/ontology, reputation mathematics, Sybil/collusion threat, registry policy, gate design) with authors, versions, canonical URIs, sections, retrieval times and SHA-256 of archived bytes; fragments labeled where full archiving was not possible.

synthesis_and_gaps.content: Governed views agree and pass every gate and probe; the control fails exactly where gates bite. Digest view carries a documented identical-text limit. Gaps: no cyclic attack graphs, no measured operator data, threshold unvalidated, Beta primaries thin.

limitations: tracked-Git evidence only; live DB recheck required in Phase B
planning threshold stays a hypothesis (no suitable data)
Beta formulas are standard results with independent computation, not archived primary full text
holdout is lineage-isolated but author-visible, not blinded
operator workload unmeasured; no human study claimed
corpus-bounded claims: no cyclic attack graphs evaluated

claims.text: PROV defines provenance as information about entities, activities and agents usable to assess quality, reliability and trustworthiness, with derivation and versioning support.
S1-003 fixtures expose the lifecycle states that the S1-012 exclusion rules (revoked, superseded, versioned) bind to.
On the frozen 72-case matrix the document, span and digest views admit exactly the oracle independents with zero hard violations, while the reputation-only control double-counts mirror/Sybil cases.
Beta posteriors with the frozen prior grid and decay clock are computed by continued fractions and agree with exact binomial references to 1e-9 on integer parameters.
Without a logically centralized authority, Sybil attacks remain possible except under extreme resource-parity assumptions, so anchorless mutual-praise clusters must never produce enforcement.
Document and span views agree on independence decisions under shared upstream collapse; the digest view adds a documented identical-text limit and never extra safety.
The planning threshold P[theta>0.9]>=0.95 stays a hypothesis without suitable data; reported tails are hypothesis quantities, not truth probabilities.
Lineage equality proxies source dependence for MVP comparison; novel Sybil shapes may evade it.

# Archived fragment (verbatim)

Title: PROV-Overview — An Overview of the PROV Family of Documents
Editors: Paul Groth (VU University Amsterdam), Luc Moreau (University
of Southampton)

## Abstract

Provenance is information about entities, activities, and people
involved in producing a piece of data or thing, which can be used to
form assessments about its quality, reliability or trustworthiness.
The PROV Family of Documents defines a model, corresponding
serializations and other supporting definitions to enable the
inter-operable interchange of provenance information in heterogeneous
environments such as the Web.

## PROV Family of Documents

- PROV-OVERVIEW (Note), an overview of this family (this document);
- PROV-PRIMER (Note), a primer for the PROV data model;
- PROV-O (Recommendation), the PROV ontology, an OWL2 ontology allowing
  the mapping of the PROV data model to RDF;
- PROV-DM (Recommendation), the PROV data model for provenance;
- PROV-N (Recommendation), a notation for provenance aimed at human
  consumption;
- PROV-CONSTRAINTS (Recommendation), constraints applying to the PROV
  data model;
- PROV-XML (Note), an XML schema for the PROV data model;
- PROV-AQ (Note), mechanisms for accessing and querying provenance;
- PROV-DICTIONARY (Note), key-entity pair collections;
- PROV-DC (Note), mapping between PROV-O and Dublin Core Terms;
- PROV-SEM (Note), declarative first-order-logic specification;
- PROV-LINKS (Note), linking across bundles.

## 1. Introduction (excerpt)

"Provenance is information about entities, activities, and people
involved in producing a piece of data or thing, which can be used to
form assessments about its quality, reliability or trustworthiness. ...
At its core is a conceptual data model (PROV-DM), which defines a
common vocabulary used to describe provenance."

"The design of PROV stems from the recommendations of the Provenance
Incubator Group ... 8 broad recommendations were defined. Summarizing,
the report recommends that a provenance framework should support: the
core concepts of identifying an object, attributing the object to
person or entity, and representing processing steps; ... the provenance
of provenance; reproducibility; versioning; representing procedures;
and representing derivation."

## 3. Namespace

"All terms defined within PROV are defined within the namespace
http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#. The prefix convention that is used is
prov."
sources.title: PROV-Overview (W3C NOTE 2013-04-30)

# Archived fragment (verbatim)

Title: The Sybil Attack
Author: John (JD) Douceur
Venue: Proceedings of 1st International Workshop on Peer-to-Peer
Systems (IPTPS) | January 2002

## Abstract (verbatim)

"Large-scale peer-to-peer systems face security threats from faulty or
hostile remote computing elements. To resist these threats, many such
systems employ redundancy. However, if a single faulty entity can
present multiple identities, it can control a substantial fraction of
the system, thereby undermining this redundancy. One approach to
preventing these 'Sybil attacks' is to have a trusted agency certify
identities. This paper shows that, without a logically centralized
authority, Sybil attacks are always possible except under extreme and
unrealistic assumptions of resource parity and coordination among
entities."
sources.title: The Sybil Attack (IPTPS 2002)

      "id": "claim-platform-target",
      "text": "Adopt an append-only, claim-scoped promotion queue with explicit status, provenance, independence, contradiction, and expiry fields for later Stage 1 tickets.",
      "claim_class": "target"
    }
  ],
  "artifacts": {
    "research_plan": {
      "content": "# Research question\nWhat targeted verification and promotion policy is sufficient for decision-critical u sources without implying that all 176 historical u records were verified?\n\n# Method\nFreeze a 12-record queue derived from downstream Stage 1 decisions; review canonical publisher or author pages; record canonical_source_id, publisher_id, independence_group, original status, proposed status, verifier, method, and corrections; test mirror/Sybil and missing-provenance near misses.\n\n# Scope\nF8, F16, F18, F19, I1, I2, I8, I14, J13, SV2, SV3, and Z13. Three tail records are explicitly covered.\n\n# Non-scope\nNo live retrieval adapter is added, no historical registry row is edited in place, and the remaining u population is not asserted verified.\n\n# Stop rule\nBlock a promotion if identity is ambiguous, fewer than two independent canonical groups support a high-risk claim, or the queue expands into mass verification.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-target-queue", "claim-history-limit", "claim-platform-target"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "source_registry": {
      "content": "# Status policy\n- v: canonical or primary source verified for the exact scoped claim, with dated verifier provenance.\n- c: verified context or contradiction source; not sufficient alone for a high-risk claim.\n- u: unresolved or missing verifier provenance; remains unpromoted.\n- x: identity/content invalid or unavailable for the scoped claim.\n- x-excluded: deliberately outside scope, with an explicit exclusion rationale.\n\nHarness-level verification_status=verified means this run verified the record and its provenance. Policy-level promotion_decision=v or c is stored separately, so c is not silently upgraded to v.\n\n# Queue\n| ID | Original | Proposed | Publisher | Independence group | Note |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| F8 | u | v | w3c | w3c-prov-working-group | canonical provenance standard |\n| F16 | u | v | elsevier-artificial-intelligence | doyle-tms | corrected DOI preserved |\n| F18 | u | v | elsevier-artificial-intelligence | dung-argumentation-framework | distinct canonical work |\n| F19 | u | v | taylor-francis-jancl | prakken-sartor-defeasible-priorities | journal/DOI correction preserved |\n| I1 | u | v | owasp-genai | owasp-genai-taxonomy | dated 2025 baseline |\n| I2 | u | v | owasp-genai | owasp-genai-taxonomy | same group as I1/Z13 |\n| I8 | u | v | cncf-in-toto | cncf-in-toto | independent supply-chain standard |\n| I14 | u | c | cloudflare | cloudflare-vendor | vendor design context only |\n| J13 | u | c | evan-miller | evan-miller-rating-method | calibration context only |\n| SV2 | u | v | arxiv | sv2-author-group | tail spot check |\n| SV3 | u | v | arxiv | sv3-author-group | tail spot check and title correction |\n| Z13 | u | v | owasp-genai | owasp-genai-taxonomy | tail spot check |\n\n# Independence\nDifferent URLs or publisher labels do not create independence. Mirrors inherit the canonical source's group. Multiple OWASP pages add coverage but count once for independence. Shared publisher alone does not collapse distinct canonical author works, but the grouping rationale must be recorded.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-target-queue", "claim-independence-policy", "claim-context-policy"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "feature_catalog": {
      "content": "# Downstream enablement\nThe promotion queue is an evidence-control feature used before later tickets cite a source. Knowledge-gate work consumes F16/F18/F19; provenance and lineage work consumes F8/I8; security work consumes I1/I2/I14/Z13; protocol work consumes SV2/SV3; calibration work may use J13 only as context.\n\n# Required fields\nEvery queue item carries claim_scope, original_status, proposed_status, canonical_source_id, canonical_uri, publisher_id, independence_group, verifier, verification_method, verified_at, correction_note, contradiction_refs, and expiry_or_refresh_rule.\n\n# Exclusions\nThe feature does not fetch pages, infer independence from domains, or promote a source merely because metadata looks plausible.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-target-queue", "claim-platform-target", "claim-context-policy"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "architecture_models": {
      "content": "# Control flow\nHistorical registry (append-only input) -> bounded candidate queue -> identity resolution -> provenance verification -> independence grouping -> claim-specific decision v/c/u/x/x-excluded -> immutable decision event -> downstream admissibility query.\n\n# Authority boundary\nThe verifier proposes evidence; a policy gate computes admissibility. Retrieved text is untrusted and cannot alter thresholds, status vocabulary, scope, or capabilities. A correction creates a new decision event linked to the erroneous prior value.\n\n# Storage boundary\nCanonical state belongs in the AgentOS DB and evidence pack. Obsidian is a deterministic readable projection. The DeepeekHarness historical registry remains unchanged by this ticket.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-independence-policy", "claim-platform-target", "claim-history-limit"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "mental_model": {
      "content": "# Human-readable decision card\nShow the exact claim, current status, original status, canonical identity, independent groups, corroborators, contradiction/context sources, corrections, verifier/method/date, and why the threshold passed or failed.\n\n# Avoid misleading signals\nDo not display a raw URL count as source diversity. Group OWASP-family records together, label vendor notes as c, and visibly retain F16/F19 metadata corrections. Use '12 targeted records reviewed' rather than '176 sources verified'.\n\n# Operator actions\nAn operator can approve the bounded queue, request another independent group, downgrade to c/u, exclude with rationale, or stop on ambiguous identity.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-independence-policy", "claim-context-policy", "claim-history-limit"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "ontology": {
      "content": "# Classes\nSourceRecord, CanonicalSource, Publisher, IndependenceGroup, ClaimScope, VerificationEvent, PromotionDecision, CorrectionEvent, MirrorRelation, ContradictionRelation, and ExclusionDecision.\n\n# Status semantics\nv and c are positive but non-equivalent policy decisions; u is unresolved; x is unusable for the scoped claim; x-excluded is intentionally out of scope. Harness verified is evidence about the verification event, not an alias for policy v.\n\n# Relations\nSourceRecord identifies CanonicalSource; CanonicalSource publishedBy Publisher; CanonicalSource memberOf IndependenceGroup; VerificationEvent evaluatedFor ClaimScope; PromotionDecision basedOn VerificationEvent; MirrorRelation inheritsCanonicalIdentity; CorrectionEvent supersedes but never erases the prior assertion.\n\n# Invariants\nEvery promotion candidate has exactly one canonical_source_id, publisher_id, and independence_group. A mirror cannot introduce a new independence group. Every v/c decision has dated verifier provenance.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-independence-policy", "claim-platform-target", "claim-target-queue"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "mathematical_model": {
      "content": "# Admission rule\nFor candidate source s and claim q, admissible_v(s,q)=1 only when identity_resolved=1, provenance_complete=1, primary_or_canonical=1, and no blocking contradiction exists. Context-only evidence yields c, not v.\n\n# High-risk claim support\nLet G(q) be unique independence groups among admissible supporters and N(q) be distinct canonical sources. Promotion of a high-risk claim requires |G(q)| >= 2 and N(q) >= 3, where the third item may be context or contradiction evidence. URL count is never used.\n\n# Mirror probe\nIf m mirrors s, canonical_source_id(m)=canonical_source_id(s) and independence_group(m)=independence_group(s); therefore adding m changes neither |G(q)| nor N(q). Expected delta is 0.\n\n# Queue bounds\nThis run has 12 candidates and 3 tail spot checks. Coverage is 12/12 for the frozen queue and explicitly not 176/176 for the historical u population.\n\n# Refresh\nA decision expires or is rechecked when canonical identity changes, a contradiction arrives, a downstream claim expands, or its ticket-defined freshness interval elapses.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-independence-policy", "claim-target-queue", "claim-history-limit"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "synthesis_and_gaps": {
      "content": "# Result\nAdopt the bounded promotion policy. Ten queue records qualify as scoped v and two vendor/practitioner records (I14, J13) qualify as c. The decision is claim-specific and does not rewrite the historical source registry.\n\n# Corrections\nF16's earlier DOI was a plausible near-miss; the correct DOI ends 90008-0. F19's earlier journal/DOI attribution was wrong; the canonical record is Journal of Applied Non-Classical Logics with DOI 10.1080/11663081.1997.10510900. SV3's current arXiv title differs from the historical local title. All three corrections retain the earlier value as error provenance.\n\n# Gaps\nNo external human auditor participated in this run. Source content was reviewed at canonical pages and metadata level, not reproduced or archived in full. Availability and freshness can change. The remaining historical u population is deliberately unresolved.\n\n# Next actions\nImplement the queue schema and exact independence gate before downstream tickets consume promotions; obtain external audit when S1-020 closes the portfolio; refresh any source when its downstream claim changes.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-target-queue", "claim-context-policy", "claim-history-limit", "claim-platform-target"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "independent_audit": {
      "content": "# Adversarial review\nThe verifier pass treated every promotion as suspect and recomputed the queue from source identity, publisher, independence group, and dated provenance. It found no claim that all 176 historical u records were verified.\n\n# Probe 1: mirror/Sybil\nA synthetic mirror with a different host and publisher label but the same canonical_source_id and independence_group produced delta |G|=0 and delta N=0. PASS: it cannot satisfy the threshold. The three OWASP records likewise count as one independence group.\n\n# Probe 2: plausible metadata without provenance\nA plausible u title with no verifier or method remains u. F16's wrong DOI and F19's wrong venue/DOI were not silently accepted; corrected identities are new scoped decisions with the old values preserved in correction_note. PASS.\n\n# Coverage checks\nAll 12 frozen candidates contain canonical_source_id, publisher_id, and independence_group; SV2, SV3, and Z13 cover the required tail spot checks; all five policy status classes are defined. High-risk evidence clusters have at least three sources and at least two independent canonical groups.\n\n# Verdict\nPASS_WITH_LIMITS. The audit role is distinct from the subject producer and used an adversarial pass, but it is not an external human or independently operated model. Portfolio closure must preserve that limit and may request external confirmation.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-independence-policy", "claim-target-queue", "claim-history-limit"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-independent-verifier"
    },
    "platform_plan": {
      "content": "# Scope\nImplement only the promotion queue, append-only decision records, exact independence computation, and downstream admissibility query. Do not add retrieval adapters or mass-verify the historical registry.\n\n# Architecture\nAdd canonical SourceIdentity, VerificationEvent, PromotionDecision, and CorrectionEvent records to canonical storage. The gate owns status transitions; retrieved documents remain untrusted inputs. Wiki pages are projections with links to claims, sources, decisions, and corrections.\n\n# Workstreams\n1. Schema and migration for claim-scoped status and provenance. 2. Canonicalization and mirror grouping. 3. Deterministic v/c/u/x/x-excluded gate. 4. Queue UI/wiki projection. 5. Regression fixtures for DOI/title corrections and Sybil mirrors. 6. Downstream query API.\n\n# Milestones\nM1 freezes the field contract and fixtures. M2 persists append-only decisions and corrections. M3 enforces independence and status gates. M4 emits evidence pack/wiki links. M5 integrates S1-009 through S1-012 consumers after their dependencies pass.\n\n# Verification\nRequire 12/12 queue-field completeness, exact grouping for OWASP and mirrors, both adversarial probes green, no historical-registry mutation, evidence-pack v3 with fresh chain/latest evaluation, and wiki-check ok=true. High-risk claims require at least three canonical sources across at least two independence groups.\n\n# Risks\nPublisher consolidation can look like dependence; authorship overlap may be missed; vendor pages can change; a verified record can be over-generalized beyond its claim scope; an operator may confuse harness verified with policy v. Mitigate with explicit scope, grouping rationale, content hashes, corrections, and expiry.\n\n# Open decisions\nChoose the refresh interval per source class; decide whether S1-020 requires an external human auditor; define acceptable canonical archive snapshots; decide how later tickets request a promotion without changing this frozen queue.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-platform-target", "claim-independence-policy", "claim-context-policy", "claim-history-limit"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    },
    "progress": {
    "content": "# 2026-08-28\nStatus: PASS_WITH_LIMITS recorded by the canonical research-plan evaluation. Frozen queue: 12/12 candidates verified for the scoped claims. Tail checks: SV2, SV3, Z13. The evidence pack and Obsidian projection were generated with a fresh audit chain.\n\nCorrections discovered: F16 DOI near-miss, F19 venue/DOI mismatch, and SV3 title drift; prior values remain preserved in provenance. The mirror/Sybil and missing-provenance probes passed.\n\nDeclared limits remain binding: no mass verification of 176 historical u entries, no external human auditor, no live retrieval adapter, and no production claim. The ticket is complete at PASS_WITH_LIMITS; external confirmation is portfolio follow-up work.",
      "claim_refs": ["claim-target-queue", "claim-history-limit", "claim-platform-target"],
      "producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer"
    }
  },
  "audit": {
    "subject_producer": "agentos-s1-001-producer",
    "auditor": "agentos-s1-001-independent-verifier",
    "verdict": "pass_with_limits",
    "limitations": [
      "The auditor role is process-separated and adversarial but is not an external human or independently operated model.",
      "The run verifies the frozen 12-record queue only; it does not verify all 176 historical u records.",
      "Canonical pages and metadata were reviewed live, but full third-party content was not archived in this repository."
    ]
  }
}

{

  "meaning_of_promoted": "PROMOTED means only that the assertion passed the versioned governance gate for the stated scope and policy version. It is NOT objective truth.",
  "actor_roles": {
    "worker": {
      "may": [
        "propose_assertion",
        "submit_evidence",

      ],
      "may_not": [
        "transition",
        "cross_scope_read"
      ]

  },
  "states": {
    "PROPOSED": {
      "terminal": false,
      "in_derived_view": false
    },
    "PROMOTED": {
      "terminal": false,
      "in_derived_view": true
    },
    "CHALLENGED": {
      "terminal": false,
      "in_derived_view": false
    },
    "REJECTED": {
      "terminal": true,
      "in_derived_view": false
    },

      "terminal": true,

    {

  },
  "challenge": {
    "opens": "Any wellformed in-scope challenge moves PROMOTED to CHALLENGED immediately and removes the claim from the eligible derived view.",

    "sla_hypothesis": "Resolution expected within operator SLA window; expiry sustains the challenge and retracts (model estimate, NOT a human study; handoff S1-013)."
  },
  "retraction_revocation_supersession": {

    "concurrency": "Concurrent promote/challenge or duplicate idempotency keys resolve to exactly one active decision; challenge is never lost; transition+audit commit atomically or not at all.",
    "idempotency": "Duplicate idempotency_key returns the recorded decision without creating a new one."
  },
  "fail_closed": [
    "missing_provenance",
    "missing_policy_version",
    "missing_actor_authority",
    "missing_evidence_binding",
    "missing_transition_reason",
    "revoked_source",
    "cross_scope_access",
    "unknown_transition",
    "stale_epoch"
  ],
  "reason_codes": [
    "THRESHOLD_MET",
    "THRESHOLD_NOT_MET",
    "EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT",
    "EVIDENCE_CORRELATED",
    "CHALLENGE_OPENED",

    "CONCURRENT_RESOLVED",
    "UNKNOWN_TRANSITION",
    "MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD",
    "INVALID_EVIDENCE_BINDING"
  ],
  "external_content": "External documents/tool output are untrusted: claims of verified/promoted/resolved, policy or capability change requests, and Goal acceptance announcements cause NO transition; the case is quarantined.",
  "migration_expiry_rollback": {
    "migration": "Adopting a richer model later replays the immutable history through the new gate; past decisions are re-evaluated, never edited.",
    "expiry": "Decisions bind to policy_version; a policy change expires standing PROMOTED claims into re-evaluation (CHALLENGED), not silent retention.",
    "rollback": "Roll back by selecting the prior contract version and re-running the gate over preserved history; no history loss by construction."
  },
  "s1_003_alignment": "S1-003 KnowledgeAssertion lifecycle (proposed/under_review/promoted/challenged/retracted/superseded/rejected) maps onto this contract with under_review folded into PROPOSED and superseded expressed as RETRACTED+SUPERSEDES. DelegationGrant revoked maps to source_revoked handling. No S1-003 fixture contradicts this mapping.",
  "event_authority": {
    "gate_pass": [
      "governance_gate"
    ],
    "gate_fail": [
      "governance_gate"
    ],

      "worker",

    "evidence_binding": "Each evidence item must carry a 64-hex digest equal to digest(evidence_id) under the corpus digest rule, verified===true (strict boolean), non-empty lineage and independence group, matching claim version/scope, and a non-revoked source lineage.",
    "unresolved_challenge": "An open in-scope challenge blocks any promotion path.",

  }

# S1-011 decision: minimal promote/challenge gate as MVP (PASS_WITH_LIMITS)

Verdict: `PASS_WITH_LIMITS` (cap forced by the provisional independence
threshold and the absence of a human operator study; see limits below).
Phase A result: `READY_FOR_CANONICALIZATION`. No truth oracle is claimed.

Revision note: this is the R3 corrective evidence revision, measured
fresh at commit `9d4c910`. R2's nine findings are closed: explicit
evidence bindings, shared promotion predicates, stale-view exclusion,
complete case-bound ledgers, exact per-cell matrix, resolvable Git
provenance, dependency identity, raw-derived publication and simultaneous
UNKNOWN bounds. Follow-up probes also covered evidence-free reads and
the shared-path ledger identity for all three designs. See
`CORRECTIVE_R3.md`. The corpus contains 72 cases; the contract is v1.0.2.

## Recommendation

Adopt the **minimal promote/challenge gate** exactly as frozen in
`knowledge-gate-contract.json` v1.0.2 / `state-machine.json`:

- States: `PROPOSED -> PROMOTED / REJECTED / RETRACTED`,
  `PROMOTED -> CHALLENGED / RETRACTED`, `CHALLENGED -> PROMOTED (new
  decision/version) / RETRACTED`. `REJECTED` and `RETRACTED` are terminal
  and preserve immutable history.
- `PROMOTED` means only "passed the versioned governance gate for the
  stated scope/policy". It is not truth.
- Provisional evidence threshold with strict bindings: >=2 verified
  evidence records with valid digests, strict boolean verified flags,
  declared lineages and groups, >=2 distinct lineages AND >=2 groups
  (lineage-collapsed), same claim version/scope, active sources, no
  unresolved challenge or revocation, provenance/digest/policy present,
  governance-only final step. Malformed bindings fail as
  INVALID_EVIDENCE_BINDING; missing fields fail closed (no defaults).
- Authority: worker proposes/opens challenges and withdraws own
  proposals; governance gate promotes/upholds/retracts/revokes/
  supersedes; operator upholds/resolves/withdraws/revokes. External
  content never transitions anything (quarantine).
- Challenge immediately excludes the claim from the eligible derived
  view; history stays hash-verifiable in a hash-chained ledger.
  Source revocation invalidates the claim and its dependents.
  Supersession links `SUPERSEDES` and retires the old version. Derived
  claims need their own evidence and a governance decision. Duplicate
  keys and replays re-evaluate the live predicate; stale records never
  restore visibility.
- Rollback: select a prior contract version and re-run the gate over
  preserved history; nothing is ever rewritten.

## Evidence (648 rows/run, two process-separated runs, one commit/tree)

- minimal-gate: all 11 hard safety counters exactly zero,
  invalid_transition_count zero, transition exactness and view
  correctness 1.0, probes A-H pass on all seeds, confusion P/R 1.0.
- argumentation (naive grounded-style, no independence counting,
  transitive support allowed): false promotions (precision 0.448),
  probes A, D, G fail; exactness 0.778. Failure mode: single or
  correlated support suffices for IN, and parent support transitively
  promotes derived claims without their own evidence.
- tms (naive automatic revision by `tms_engine`): false promotions
  (precision 0.464), 96 ledger/authority consistency violations across
  merged seeds plus authority expansions, probes A, D, G fail. Failure
  modes: same acceptability weakness plus view-changing transitions
  with no governance decision.
- All three: recall 1.0 (no valid promotion missed), probes B/C/E/F/H
  pass (shared strict plumbing holds).
- Sensitivity: 20 per-weight (+-50%) sweeps + 200 seeded normalized
  compositions, 0 winner flips, UNKNOWN disclosure clean
  (unknown_dependent=false). The winner is robust because measured
  safety dimensions floor minimal-gate above any permitted reweighting.
  Hard-failed designs are excluded before ranking; an all-fail field
  would yield BLOCKED, never "best of the unsafe".

## Why not the richer models now

Both alternatives fail hard invariants in their textbook (naive) form,
not because of implementation bugs: acceptability without independence
binding promotes correlated/Sybil support, and automatic revision
bypasses governance authority. Hardening either (independence binding +
authority binding + UNDECIDED/backtracking operator procedure) is real
work that converges toward the minimal gate plus a graph cache. That
work is deferred, not denied (see handoffs). This resolves G-06 for the
MVP boundary: argumentation/TMS are rarely production-tested here
because their naive forms are unsafe under the frozen invariants.

## Limits (transferred, must gate production)

1. Provisional threshold is uncalibrated: real independence,
   correlation/Sybil resistance and evidence-unit calibration are
   S1-012. Any production use before S1-012 stays blocked; this task
   caps at `PASS_WITH_LIMITS`.
2. Operator workload is a model/simulation estimate, not a human study.
   Comprehension and approval fatigue are S1-013; explainability stays
   utility-estimated until then.
3. No SHACL mapping exists yet for attack/support/justification
   relations (ontology_shacl_fit abstains for both alternatives); S1-003
   alignment holds only for the minimal mapping.
4. Argumentation cycles never occur in the corpus (no cyclic attack
   graphs); convergence behavior on hostile graphs is UNKNOWN.
5. Phase A is worktree evidence. Live DB consistency, artifact-chain
   freshness and wiki checks are a separate Phase B result; consult
   `../evaluation-record.json` for canonical publication. Neither phase
   proves production persistence, distributed concurrency or human UX.

## Rollback without history loss

Re-select any prior contract version; replay immutable history through
its gate; past decisions are re-evaluated, never edited (contract
section `migration_expiry_rollback`). The corpus, runner and evaluator
are deterministic, so any rollback decision is exactly reproducible.
